source.title: NeuroBreak: Unveil Internal Jailbreak Mechanisms in Large Language Models
source.authors: Chu-Han Zhang; Ye Zhang; Bowen Shi; Yu-You Gan; Tianyu Du; Shou-Ling Ji; Da-Zhang Deng; Yingcai Wu

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates jailbreak outcomes and uses neuron-masking interventions to test safety-related behavior, but does not use the original studies’ fine-tuning or token-position KL methods.
record.gate_note: Tests jailbreak attacks, including GCG, and tests the effect of masking identified neurons on safety scores. It does not test harmful- or benign-example fine-tuning as a safety-eroding intervention, aligned-versus-base per-token KL, compliant-prefix prefilling, decoding changes, or why safety would be shallow. The reported probe accuracies are not results for the claim versions. The paper cites results from prior work, which are not recorded as rows. Some results are only described qualitatively in the text or shown in figures without extractable numeric values.
record.test_reason: The study masks small sets of identified 'dedicated safety neurons' (top 1% safety-important minus top 1% utility-important) in Llama-3-8B-Instruct and reports the change in safety score (1−ASR). That is a different method aimed at V5's question. Its jailbreak evaluations use template and rewrite attacks (AutoDan, HJB, TAP, GPT-Fuzzer) plus GCG. GCG ASR on the untreated model appears only in a figure, and there is no prefilling or decoding test, so V4 is not tested from the text. Its targeted fine-tuning results are evaluations of its own defense method against baselines.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that NeuroBreak's layer-wise probing and neuron character–behavior analysis reveal non-obvious safety mechanisms under jailbreaks: mid-layer tipping points, cross-layer regulatory neurons and reversal neurons. They also conclude that expert-guided targeted fine-tuning of about 0.2% of parameters turns these insights into measurable defense gains while keeping utility.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses jailbreak evaluation, layer-wise linear probes, neuron attribution and masking, and targeted safety fine-tuning; it does not reproduce the cited harmful/benign fine-tuning or aligned-versus-base token-position KL methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports variation across attack families and across local versus global neuron interventions. It also reports different outcomes for uniformly selected versus expert-guided targeted fine-tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear probes show successful and failed jailbreaks diverging in harmfulness representation at mid layers (around Layer 11). Probe accuracy runs from 76% in shallow layers to 93% in later layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jailbreak success versus failure is decided at a mid-layer representational tipping point.

fits_no_version.finding: Some neurons switch from benign to harmful contextual contribution under successful jailbreaks ('reversal neurons'); upweighting them in targeted tuning improved defense.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jailbreaks flip the contextual role of specific safety neurons.

record.problems: Quantitative evaluations focus on Llama-3-8B-Instruct and English jailbreak settings; the authors identify language scope and manual exploration as limitations. The text reports no uncertainty estimates. Several treatment results are only presented in figures, whose numeric values are not extractable from the supplied text. Neuron counts for global masking are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows omitted. The text describes local neuron-masking effects mainly as representation shifts rather than direct harmful-compliance rates; these were not recorded as direct behavioral results for V5. Numeric treatment values referenced in Figs. 9–10 are not available in the supplied text.

untested.parts: No aligned-vs-base per-token KL or token-position analysis. The layer-wise analysis is over layers, not response positions.
No prefilling or decoding manipulation. GCG suffix ASR on the untreated model is figure-only. No first-token mechanism is isolated.
Low-rank localization is not tested. Neuron counts are unstated. Only one model (Llama-3-8B-Instruct); the 70B model is mentioned only for latency.
No training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens. The targeted neuron fine-tuning is not position-deepening, and its durability is not tested.

missing.what: Masking AutoDan-identified safety neurons lowered defense against HJB and GPT-Fuzzer much more than against TAP. This is cross-attack evidence on localization, reported qualitatively.
missing.locator: §7.1.2 'Comparing Attack Patterns Across Jailbreak Methods', Fig. 8-B1

missing.what: Safety score/ASR of the untreated Llama-3-8B-Instruct under each attack, including the GCG suffix attack. Figure-only in Fig. 7-A1/Fig. 9.

record.verdict_notes: This is a visual-analytics paper. The V5 evidence comes from single-session expert case studies on one model and 100-instance sets, with no uncertainty reported. Neuron counts and exact masked-set sizes are not given. Wei et al. (pruning/low-rank brittleness) is cited as the basis for safety neurons but is not an original source here. Most of the quantitative results (Fig. 9) are figure-only and concern the authors' defense method.

versions.untested_parts: Whether fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred harmful examples makes a safety-trained model comply.
Whether ordinary or carefully selected benign fine-tuning data increases harmful compliance.
The aligned-versus-base per-token KL distribution across response positions.
The study evaluates several jailbreak attack families, including GCG, but does not test compliant-start prefilling or decoding changes, and does not isolate a first-token mechanism.
The number of neurons involved in the reported global masks is not stated; the study does not test low-rank edits.
Whether the data or training objective causes safety shallowness.
Whether training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens deepens safety or how such safety holds up.

rows.subject: Llama-3-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated jailbreak vulnerability under AutoDan using the safety score (1 − ASR).

conditions.value: attack-enhanced SALAD-Bench; 100 sampled instances for analysis

rows.note: The text says AutoDan reduced the safety score to 0.66. The value indicates vulnerability under this attack, but does not isolate a compliant opening or first-token bypass.
rows.check: AutoDan is a generated template/prompt-rewrite jailbreak, not a prefilled compliant opening, suffix or decoding change. The value 0.66 (safety score) is also used to select the attack for the case study. It does not bear on V4's opening-bypass mechanism.

rows.subject: Llama-3-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Disabled blue-region neurons across all layers during inference.
rows.note: The paper reports a drop from 0.6 to 0.2 and describes minimal utility loss. The number of neurons masked is not stated.
rows.check: Correctly linked. The neuron set is the default dedicated-safety set (p=q=0.01, i.e. top 1% safety-important minus utility neurons), but the exact count is not stated. Single model, case-study observation, no uncertainty reported.

rows.subject: Llama-3-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Disabled red-region neurons across all layers during inference.
rows.locator: §7.1.1, “Refining the intuition into a cross-layer regulatory mechanism”
rows.note: The paper says the global intervention lowered the safety score to 0.5, despite a local Layer 32 intervention moving samples farther from the decision boundary. The global baseline is not explicitly given for this comparison.
rows.check: Baseline is presumably the same 0.6 as R2 but is not restated. The drop to 0.5 is much weaker than the blue-region drop to 0.2. Local Layer-32 red masking moved samples away from the boundary, i.e. increased safety locally.

rows.subject: Llama-3-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated after LoRA fine-tuning against jailbreak attacks.

conditions.value: SALAD-Bench; 100 evaluation instances for the attack

rows.note: The authors describe LoRA as remaining vulnerable to complex attacks. This reports attack success, not a test of compliant-start prefilling.
rows.check: Comparator from the study's own defense-method comparison: ASR of a LoRA safety-fine-tuned model. This is not a measure of the original model's bypassability and should not be a claim row.

rows.subject: Llama-3-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated after LoRA fine-tuning against jailbreak attacks.

conditions.value: SALAD-Bench; 100 evaluation instances for the attack

rows.note: GCG is among the evaluated jailbreak methods. The paper does not give a no-LoRA comparison for this value in the text.
rows.check: Same as R4. This is the LoRA-defended model's GCG ASR, a method-comparison value with no untreated baseline in the text.

rows.subject: Llama-3-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned identified dedicated safety neurons uniformly.

conditions.value: one epoch ASR and utility; figure reports results

rows.value: The text says it achieved stronger overall defense while maintaining competitive utility; exact values are figure-only.
rows.note: This targeted intervention updates a small parameter fraction, but does not establish that the same parameters exclusively carry safety behavior. Numeric results for this treatment are not available in the supplied text.
rows.check: The study's own method (NeuroBreakAuto) performance versus baselines. The values are figure-only. It is a defense/mitigation result, not a measure of safety localization.

rows.subject: Llama-3-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned safety-neuron candidates while upweighting harmful-character reversal neurons and their gradient-linked upstream neurons.

conditions.value: one epoch ASR and utility; figure reports results

rows.value: The text says it performed best overall while maintaining competitive utility; exact values are figure-only.
rows.note: The authors also state that this variant converged faster and had lower loss than NeuroBreakAuto over 7 epochs (Fig. 10); those training-loss results are not a direct safety-behavior measure.
rows.check: The study's own method (NeuroBreakGuided) performance versus baselines. The values are figure-only.
